source_claims.claim: For bounded f on [a,b] and Stieltjes measure function alpha with mu({a}) = 0, f is Riemann-Stieltjes integrable on [a,b] iff f is continuous mu-almost everywhere on the interval.
If f is Riemann-Stieltjes integrable on [a,b], then f is integrable with respect to the completion of the induced Lebesgue-Stieltjes measure over [a,b].
If f is Riemann-Stieltjes integrable on [a,b], then the Riemann-Stieltjes integral equals the completed Lebesgue-Stieltjes integral over [a,b].

claim_mapping.assumptions: hab : a < b, hBounded : exists M, forall x in Icc a b, abs (f x) <= M, hAtom : alpha.measure {a} = 0
claim_mapping.conclusion: RSIntegrable f alpha a b iff forall-ae x under alpha.measure.restrict (Icc a b), ContinuousWithinAt f (Icc a b) x

claim_mapping.lean_declaration: prob_7_3_partB_completion_integrable_integral_eq; public theorem prob_7_3 second conjunct first component
claim_mapping.assumptions: same source assumptions plus hRS : RSIntegrable f alpha a b
claim_mapping.conclusion: IntegrableOn (fun x : NullMeasurableSpace Real alpha.measure => f x) (Icc a b) alpha.measure.completion

claim_mapping.conclusion: rsIntegral f alpha a b hRS equals the set integral over Icc a b of the NullMeasurableSpace-lifted function against alpha.measure.completion

Conversely, a.e. continuity gives null large-oscillation layers, small open neighborhoods of closed layers, compact-complement uniform small oscillation, DarbouxGapSmall, and hence RSIntegrable. Part (b) derives AEStronglyMeasurable and ordinary IntegrableOn from part (a), boundedness, and finite restricted measure; proves the Ioc Darboux sandwich equality; uses hAtom to pass from Ioc to Icc; and transfers integrability and the set integral to Measure.completion using trim APIs.
